answers.answer: For 2/3/4 players, deal 4/3/2 Player cards each. Remove the Epidemic cards and set them aside before shuffling and dealing the remaining City and Event cards. Each player's pawn starts in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 5–6: remove Epidemic cards; 2/3/4 players get 4/3/2 cards; matching pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2. Flip 3 Infection cards and put 3 matching cubes on each named city; flip 3 more and put 2 each; flip 3 more and put 1 each. Put all nine revealed cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; the remaining cards form the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 8: leftmost “2”; 3/3/3 cards receive 3/2/1 cubes; nine face up in discard, remainder Infection Deck.

answers.answer: Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemics. Divide the remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles as equal in size as possible, shuffle one Epidemic into each pile, then stack the piles with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: difficulty counts and pile preparation; smaller piles on the bottom.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; actions may repeat and you may stop early. Action-cost cards go to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve Epidemics before discarding/playing Events to the hand limit, then Infect Cities. After all three phases, play passes left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Actions: up to 4 actions, repeat or stop; action cards to Player Discard Pile; draw, infect, then pass left.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry moves along a white connecting line and costs no card. Direct Flight discards the City card of the destination. Charter Flight discards the City card matching the city you are in to move anywhere. Shuttle Flight requires departure from a city with a research station and moves to any other station city. White lines wrapping off a board edge connect to the other edge (example: Sydney–Los Angeles).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions table; Special Rules: “White lines going off one edge ... wrap to the other edge.”

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a station from the supply, and place it in that city. If all six are built, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If the box supplied more than six, set extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, Build a Research Station; Special Rules: only 6 exist; set extras aside during setup.

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action by a non-Medic removes one cube of one chosen color; because each of the two cured colors is treated separately, each requires its own action to remove all cubes of that color from the city. The uncured color is also treated one cube per action, with further actions needed as applicable. Removed cubes return to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Treat Disease: remove 1 cube; if cured, return all cubes of that one color; different colors require separate actions; cubes return to supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of one disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease's cure marker to its Cure Indicator; the station city's color need not match. Existing cubes remain, and the disease can still get cubes from infections or Epidemics until eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board, it is immediately eradicated and its marker is flipped.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: any station; 5 same-color cards, 4 for Scientist; existing cubes remain; no cubes means immediate eradication.

answers.answer: Normally, give or take the City card matching the city both players occupy. Both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they immediately discard or play an Event card until within the limit.
answers.evidence: Share Knowledge action and Hand Limit: matching current-city card; both agree; immediate hand-limit adjustment.

answers.answer: The Researcher may give any City card from their hand to a player in the same city, on either player's turn. The exception only allows cards from the Researcher to the other player; it does not let another player give an arbitrary nonmatching City card to the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Researcher exception: any card from Researcher, either player's turn; does not allow arbitrary cards given to Researcher.

answers.answer: After actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when the draw is needed, the game ends and players lose; do not reshuffle discards.
answers.evidence: Drawing Player Cards: draw top 2 together; if fewer than 2 remain when you need to draw, lose; do not reshuffle discards.

answers.answer: First increase the Infection Rate by one. Draw the bottom Infection card; since the city has two matching cubes, add one to reach three and an outbreak occurs. Advance the Outbreaks marker and spread one cube of that color to connected cities, observing chain-reaction rules. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile, then Intensify by reshuffling only that pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game; do not draw a replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, steps 1–3: increase, draw bottom and reach 3 then outbreak, discard, intensify; Epidemic removed with no replacement.

answers.answer: After 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6 Epidemics, flip 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, and 4 Infection cards, respectively.
answers.evidence: Infection Rate Track table: positions after 0–6 epidemics map to 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 cards.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic's three steps completely, then the second's three steps. Events may be played between the two Epidemics. If over the limit, first resolve any Epidemics just drawn, then discard or play Events to reach 7 or fewer.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: two at once resolve all steps for first then second; Events between. Hand Limit: first resolve Epidemics, then reduce hand.

answers.answer: Flip the top Infection Deck cards, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For a non-eradicated disease, place one matching cube in the named city; a cured but not eradicated disease still gets cubes. For an eradicated disease place none. If the city already has three cubes of that color, place no fourth and cause an outbreak. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities: flip top cards equal to rate; eradicated disease gets no cube; 3 cubes causes outbreak; discard each card. Cure Procedure confirms cured disease can still infect.

answers.answer: During an outbreak, advance the outbreak marker, then place one cube on each connected city. If a connected city already has three of that color, its chain outbreak happens after the current outbreak resolves, advancing the marker again. Do not add cubes to any city that already had an outbreak while resolving that Infection card, so the chain does not spread back into the first city. Each color has its own cap of three; a city can contain multiple colors.
answers.evidence: Outbreaks: marker advances; connected cities get 1; chain reactions after current outbreak; no cubes to cities already outbreaking this card; up to 3 of each color.

answers.answer: No. Once an Infection card has been drawn, Airlift cannot be played between drawing and resolving that card, so it cannot move the Quarantine Specialist before that outbreak resolves. After resolving the current card, an Event may be played before the next card is drawn/resolved. Airlift is not an action; its player chooses the use, and the played Event goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: any time, not an action; cannot be played between drawing and resolving a card; player playing chooses; discard to Player Discard Pile.

answers.answer: As an action, take one Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and store it on the Contingency Planner Role card. Only one can be stored; it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.
answers.evidence: Roles, Contingency Planner: action, anywhere in Player Discard Pile, limit 1, not hand limit; on play remove from game.

answers.answer: As an action, the Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player's pawn as if their own; moving another player's pawn requires its owner's agreement. Direct/Charter Flight costs are paid from the Dispatcher's hand; the Charter card matches the moved pawn's departure city. A directed pawn may move but cannot Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions. Dispatcher cannot use the Operations Expert special move.
answers.evidence: Roles, Dispatcher: both movement options and permission; cards from Dispatcher; Charter departure city; no treating/nonmovement; cannot use Operations Expert move.

answers.answer: Win immediately when cures for all four diseases are discovered; eradication and a clear board are not required. Lose if the outbreak marker reaches its last space (8th outbreak), if the required cubes of a color cannot be placed (during Epidemics, outbreaks, or infections), or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after actions because fewer than two remain. Cube-supply inability causes immediate loss.
answers.evidence: Victory and Defeat: all four cures; eradication not required; 8 outbreaks, cube supply exhausted, or Player Deck draw failure; cube check says immediate loss.

answers.answer: Place the board and put the six research stations and separated disease cubes nearby; place one station in Atlanta; put the Outbreaks marker at 0 and the four cure markers vial side up by their indicators. Give each player a reference card; shuffle Role cards and deal one face up per player, put matching pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused roles and pawns. Put the Infection Rate marker at the leftmost 2 when infecting initial cities. Highest-population City card holder goes first.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 8–9 cover supplies, markers, roles, pawns, Atlanta, and first player; step 8 places Infection Rate marker at leftmost 2.

answers.answer: The active player decides their own actions. Introductory hands are face up; Standard/Heroic hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may inspect either discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: active player decides; Special Rules: hand visibility by difficulty and either discard pile may be examined.

answers.answer: Removing the last cube before the disease is cured does not eradicate it. If the last cube of a cured disease is removed, eradicate it and flip its cure marker to the eradication side. After eradication, no new cubes are placed during normal infections or Epidemics.
answers.evidence: Eradication: last cube of cured disease triggers flip; last cube of uncured disease has no effect; eradicated diseases receive no new cubes.

answers.answer: Place 3 matching cubes on the zero-cube city. There is no outbreak simply for reaching three; outbreak occurs if the city already has cubes and the Epidemic adds only enough to reach three. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, Infect step: place 3; if city already has cubes, add only enough to reach 3 then outbreak; discard card.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs. No cubes are placed for the eradicated disease, but the Infection card is discarded to the Infection Discard Pile and Intensify still reshuffles that pile onto the top of the Infection Deck. The Epidemic card is removed from the game and has no replacement draw.
answers.evidence: Epidemic steps; Infecting Cities says eradicated disease gets no cube; after Infect, discard card and Intensify.

answers.answer: The first Epidemic fully resolves and empties the Infection Discard Pile during Intensify. The second bottom Infection card is then the only card in the discard pile, so the second Intensify shuffles only that card and puts it on top. In the stated zero-cube, unprotected, non-eradicated city, it gets 3 cubes from the second Epidemic without an outbreak, then is drawn first during normal infections and causes an outbreak unless an effect prevents it.
answers.evidence: Two Epidemics at once: second bottom card is the only card shuffled on second Intensify; city reaches 3 and is drawn first, causing outbreak absent prevention.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 same-color City cards instead of 5 to Discover a Cure. The research-station requirement and same disease-color card requirement still apply.
answers.evidence: Cure Procedure: 4 for Scientist; Roles: Scientist needs only 4 cards of same color; cure is at a research station.

answers.answer: Operations Expert builds a research station in the city they currently occupy, as an action, without needing to hold, use, or discard a City card.
answers.evidence: Roles, Operations Expert: as an action, build a station in current city with no City card needed, used, or discarded.

answers.answer: Once per turn, as an action, Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card. The card does not have to match the destination or departure city.
answers.evidence: Roles, Operations Expert: once per turn as an action, from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.

answers.answer: For an uncured disease, the Medic's Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the Medic's city. It does not remove cubes of other colors in that same action.
answers.evidence: Roles, Medic: Treat Disease removes all cubes of one color; Other Actions specify separate actions for different colors.

answers.answer: When the cure is discovered while the Medic is already in a city with cubes of that color, remove those cubes immediately. Later, when moved into another such city via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn, the Medic automatically removes all cubes of that cured color upon entering, with no action needed. The cure-time removal also is immediate and requires no action.
answers.evidence: Roles, Medic: if already in city when cure discovered, remove immediately; entering via Dispatcher or Airlift on another player's turn triggers automatic removal.

answers.answer: The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the Medic's current city. This protection does not extend to adjacent cities and does not apply to uncured diseases.
answers.evidence: Roles, Medic: prevents cured-disease placement and outbreaks in Medic's city; no adjacent-city or uncured-disease protection.

answers.answer: The Quarantine Specialist protects the current city and every connected city from placements and outbreaks of every disease color. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.
answers.evidence: Roles, Quarantine Specialist: every color in current and connected cities; no effect on setup cubes.

answers.answer: Resilient Population removes any one card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between an Epidemic's Infect and Intensify steps, so it may remove the card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify shuffles the pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards: remove any 1 card in Infection Discard Pile from game; may be played between Infect and Intensify.

answers.answer: One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step, with no Infection cards flipped. It does not skip an Epidemic's Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, One Quiet Night: skip next Infect Cities and do not flip cards; does not skip Epidemic Infect.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any one pawn to any city. If it is another player's pawn, get that player's permission.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, Airlift: move any 1 pawn to any city; get permission for another player's pawn.

answers.answer: Only Player cards count against the 7-card limit; Role and Reference cards do not, and a stored Contingency Planner Event does not. Reduce a hand of nine by discarding cards or playing Event cards until at most seven remain (with any newly drawn Epidemics resolved first).
answers.evidence: Hand Limit: Player cards only, max 7, resolve Epidemics before discard/play; Contingency Planner stored card does not count.

answers.answer: Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of the player's location, without discarding a City card.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, Government Grant: place a research station in any city, no card discard needed.

answers.answer: Forecast lets you draw and view the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, rearrange them, and put them back on top of that deck.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, Forecast: draw, view, rearrange top 6 Infection cards, then put them back on top.
